title: Energy-Flow Cosmology: Regime-Transition Fit to DESI DR2 BAO
description: Validates a minimal Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) regime-transition parameterization against DESI DR2 BAO using a transparent manual likelihood and a covariance-aware conditional hold-out test. The model modifies E^2(z) by a tanh transition modulated by (1+z)^{-1}, achieves a large Δχ^2 = −22.01 improvement over ΛCDM for two extra parameters, and remains consistent with Pantheon+ SNe (after M-marginalization) and cosmic chronometers. Combined BAO+CC information criteria favor the EFC transition model (ΔBIC ≈ −14.5).

modified_friedmann_transition.description: Minimal EFC regime-transition parameterization that rescales the background expansion; reduces exactly to ΛCDM when \alpha_{L2}=0.

coupling_function.description: Phenomenological redshift dependence of the energy-flow coupling.

transition_function.description: Smooth tanh transition centered at z_{L1L2} with fixed width Δz.

bao_likelihood.description: Covariance-aware χ^2 for DESI DR2 BAO using DV/rs, DM/rs, DH/rs.

sn_marginalized_likelihood.description: Analytic marginalization over the absolute magnitude M for supernovae.

conditional_holdout.description: Covariance-aware conditional hold-out test accounting for cross-covariance between training (t) and hold-out (h) subsets.

key_results.main_finding: DESI DR2 BAO strongly favor an EFC tanh-transition at z_L1L2 ≈ 1 with coupling α_L2 ≈ 0.045, yielding Δχ^2 = −22.01 for two extra parameters and surviving a covariance-aware conditional hold-out (Δχ^2_h|t = −18.65), while Pantheon+ and H(z) chronometers remain consistent.
datasets_used: DESI DR2 BAO (13 points; DV/rs, DM/rs, DH/rs)

sealed_predictions.statement: Independent BAO compilations (e.g., DESI DR3/DR4, BOSS/eBOSS reanalyses) fit with the same two-parameter EFC model (Δz = 0.3, Planck 2018 priors) will prefer a single transition near z_L1L2 = 1.0 ± 0.2 with a positive coupling 0.03 ≤ α_L2 ≤ 0.06 and yield ΔBIC ≤ −6 relative to ΛCDM.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Re-fitting future or independent BAO datasets with identical likelihood and priors; failure to achieve ΔBIC ≤ −6 or preference for α_L2 ≈ 0 within uncertainties falsifies this prediction.

sealed_predictions.statement: After analytic M-marginalization, the supernova distance-modulus residual shape relative to ΛCDM, Δμ_shape(z), remains |Δμ_shape(z)| < 0.002 mag over 0.01 < z < 2.3 for the EFC best-fit parameters.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: A Pantheon+-like reanalysis with full covariance showing |Δμ_shape(z)| ≥ 0.002 mag over any contiguous Δz ≥ 0.3 interval.

kill_criteria: KC1: Independent BAO datasets (e.g., DESI DR3/DR4, BOSS/eBOSS) analyzed with the same EFC parameterization (Δz = 0.3) and Planck-informed priors yield ΔBIC ≥ 0 (or ΔAIC ≥ 0) versus ΛCDM, indicating no improvement once parameter penalty is applied.

KC2: Covariance-aware conditional hold-out or K-fold cross-validation on DESI DR2 (or successor datasets) shows average Δχ^2_h|t ≥ −4 for EFC relative to ΛCDM across multiple random partitions, indicating no robust generalization gain.

KC3: High-precision H(z) measurements (e.g., improved CC or standard sirens) with σ_H/H ≤ 3% over 0.5 < z < 1.5 constrain the EFC coupling to |α_L2| < 0.01 (95% CL), placing α_L2 = 0.045 outside 3σ when combined with BAO.

KC4: Supernova datasets with full covariance and absolute calibration, after M-marginalization, exhibit a redshift-dependent residual shape |Δμ_shape(z)| ≥ 0.01 mag over 0.1 < z < 1.5 that is inconsistent with the EFC f(z)Θ(z) modulation, or strongly prefers ΛCDM over the fixed-Δz EFC model by ΔBIC ≥ 0.
KC5: Joint BAO+CC fits allowing H0 and r_d to vary within Planck 2018 priors eliminate the EFC advantage (ΔAIC ≥ 0 or ΔBIC ≥ 0) and constrain α_L2 consistent with zero at ≥ 3σ.

KC6: Cross-probe consistency fails: best-fit z_L1L2 values inferred from low-z (z < 0.8) and high-z (z > 1.2) BAO subsets disagree at > 3σ, ruling out a single-transition EFC with fixed width Δz = 0.3.
subtitle: With Cross-Validation Against Pantheon+ and H(z) Chronometers
